reasons: No tests are visible in this packet to confirm the output shape or the share rule.
The share sum rule is stated in the prompt but not checked in code here.

terms.meaning: Problems in how a process has been built up over time, scored later by a separate auditor.
A recorded difficulty in the process, linked to the steps it affects.
A step's fraction of the total effort of the process.
Real calendar time from start to finish, which can be much longer than the effort spent.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Cartographer purpose and template rules
sections.what: Explains the stage: map how the process works today and nothing more. The prompt rules say share is a fraction of effort, elapsed duration is a separate measure, roles are not named people, steps are numbered from one, and pain points link to steps.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: a model asked to describe a broken process wants to fix it, so the boundary is written down.
sections.watch_out: The prompt rules are the main control on this output, so editing them changes results without any code error.

sections.name: _CartographerOutput
sections.title: Output shape the model returns
sections.what: Defines the two parts the model returns: a list of steps and a list of pain points. It deliberately has no field for workflow debt.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: workflow debt belongs to the auditor, and a field the model is never shown cannot be filled.
sections.watch_out: Adding a debt field here would let the model write the auditor's judgement, which the design avoids.

sections.name: CurrentStateCartographer
sections.title: Cartographer setup and final assembly
sections.what: Sets the agent's name, tier, output limit and must-not rule, fills the prompt with the process brief, and builds the final current state with an empty workflow debt list.
sections.why: Stated in the code: the empty list records that this agent did not do the auditor's job.
sections.watch_out: An empty debt list means not yet assessed, not no debt. Treating it as no debt would be wrong.

summary: The stage that describes how a process works today, step by step, with who does each step, in which system, how long it takes and its share of effort, plus the pain points observed. It does not propose fixes.
purpose: Produce a factual baseline of the current process that later stages can grade and redesign against.
why: The docstring says a redesign smuggled into the description would contaminate every stage after it, so the boundary is enforced by the shape of the output.
how: 1) The prompt template asks for steps, roles, systems, durations, effort shares and pain points, and forbids proposing improvements. 2) The output shape has steps and pain points only, with no debt field. 3) The agent is set up with its name, tier, output limit and must-not rule. 4) The final current state is assembled with an empty workflow debt list.
inputs: A ProcessBrief describing one process, rendered into the prompt.
outputs: A CurrentState with steps, pain points and an empty workflow debt list for the auditor to fill later.
risks: Shares must sum to one across steps, and that rule is written only in the prompt, not checked in this file. An empty debt list is a placeholder, so code reading it as no debt found would be wrong.
debug: If the output looks like a fix, check whether the prompt wording was changed. If shares do not add up, read the prompt rules and the steps returned. If later stages see no debt, confirm the auditor ran, since this stage always leaves the list empty.
